chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: Jazz Train: bad management, Europe and Johnson's wish to revive it
summary: Harper says four shows with Johnson lacked good management; Jazz Train in Britain and Ireland drew ten-minute finales, and Johnson wants it back.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: The unfortunate part about the whole thing was that -- of the shows I worked with J. C. on -- and we did four -- we never had good management. They were either racketeers in the legitimate sense or underworld, because both

of them would manage and produce the shows, but they were only worried about profit, not artistic endeavor. And we gave them hits, but they were too big for them, much too big because since then, when we were in Europe, when we were in London -- that's before the Beatles dug us and got the beat from us and brought it over here and made $17 million (inaudible), but that's what happened.

We set them on fire. We went to Ireland, went to Scotland with our rhythm and our beat, and our finale would last ten minutes, just the finale. And they wouldn't want us to leave the stage. They would stand up and holler, 'Don't go, don't go!' And we could -- we kept doing the same step over and over and over and over.

And as a result the tension of the moment would get so that you could cut it with a knife, it would be so heavy. And J. would just stand back there and smile and say, let's go and get some tea, man. And we would -- he was --
Well, you know, that Jazz Train was the last really big show that he did.
And then he retired. He came up to work (inaudible) to the Hinterlands. But when I said to him about a year ago, you know, what you really -- anything you
want in the world, what would it be? And he said, just to bring back the Jazz Train.
